whmcs_integration.title: WHMCS integration
whmcs_integration.subtitle: If you bill hosting with WHMCS: download the server module ZIP and follow the steps below. End customers never enter API keys.
whmcs_integration.step_1: In this panel’s .env set PANELZE_WHMCS_SECRET to a long random value (e.g. openssl rand -hex 32).
whmcs_integration.step_2: Extract the ZIP. Copy the panelze folder to your WHMCS server at: whmcs_root/modules/servers/panelze/ (panelze.php must sit in that folder).
whmcs_integration.step_3: WHMCS admin → Configuration → System Settings → Servers → Add New Server and choose module panelze.
whmcs_integration.step_4: Server hostname: this panel’s URL (e.g. https://panel.example.com). Password field: same value as PANELZE_WHMCS_SECRET. Optional username: Panelze admin email (admin SSO).
whmcs_integration.step_5: Test connection. Package IDs: GET .../api/integrations/whmcs/packages with Authorization: Bearer and the same secret.
whmcs_integration.step_6: Attach your hosting product to this server; on provision the panel user and site are created automatically. WHMCS client email = panel user email.
whmcs_integration.step_7: Customer access: WHMCS client area → service details → SSO / “Open panel” (template link or WHMCS single sign-on).
whmcs_integration.footer_note: This page is admin-only. The ZIP is the current Panelze server module; re-download after panel upgrades.
whmcs_integration.deprecated_title: Native billing is now built into Panelze
whmcs_integration.deprecated_body: Orders, invoices, automatic provisioning, payment reminders, and support tickets can be managed without WHMCS. Use Billing Management for new setups; WHMCS remains optional for existing migrations only.

email.guide_step_webmail: For webmail, click Inbox on the row — Roundcube opens without typing a password (per-domain webmail.yourdomain URL).

email.guide_step_dns: For delivery, verify MX, SPF, DKIM, and DMARC on the DNS page; use Create mail DNS records on Connection to add them automatically.
email.card_incoming_body: Recommended: IMAPS port 993 (SSL/TLS). The server hostname for the selected domain is shown on Connection (often mail.yourdomain or the hosting server). For browser reading, Inbox is enough.
email.card_outgoing_body: SMTP submission: port 587 (STARTTLS) or 465 (SSL). Username is your full email address; password is the mailbox password set here — not your panel login.
email.card_panel_mail_body: Password resets and system alerts use the admin Outbound mail (SMTP) settings. Customer mailboxes are separate Postfix/Dovecot accounts.
email.ports_hint: Panelze mail stack (Postfix + Dovecot): IMAPS 993, SMTP submission 587 (STARTTLS), SMTPS 465. IMAP 143 is optional with STARTTLS.
email.auth_full_email_hint: Username is the full email address; password is the mailbox password you set here.
email.deliverability_intro: MX must point to this server; SPF, DKIM (OpenDKIM), and DMARC should be published in DNS. Reverse DNS (PTR) for the sending IP should match the server hostname. Start with low volume to providers like Gmail.
email.stack_webmail_hint: Server admin: install the “Full mail + Roundcube webmail” bundle under Admin → Server packages so webmail.* and SMTP/IMAP ports are available.
email.stack_webmail_ready: Mail server and Roundcube webmail are installed.
email.dns_hint: MX, SPF, DKIM, and DMARC are managed on the DNS page. If the domain’s nameservers are not delegated to the panel, webmail and DNS warnings may appear.
email.new_password_hint: Leave empty to keep the current password.
email.password_once: We show the new password only once — store it safely.

email.forwarders_empty: No forwarders for this domain yet.
email.forwarder_keep_copy: Keep a copy in source mailbox
email.forwarder_domain_mismatch: Source address must belong to selected domain.
email.webmail_note_body: Roundcube lives at webmail.yourdomain per domain; Inbox signs you in with one click. For desktop or mobile, use IMAP/SMTP on the Connection tab. If the mail stack is missing, an admin must install the Full mail + Roundcube webmail bundle under Server packages.
email.read_only_hint: You can only view mailboxes on this account. email:write permission is required to make changes.
email.local_part_invalid: Local part may only contain letters, digits, and . _ + - ; it cannot start or end with a special character.

cron.subtitle: Presets, custom cron expression, and quota summary
cron.info_fields: Format: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week — five fields (same order as Linux crontab).
cron.info_timezone: Times use the panel app timezone: {{tz}} (align with your server/engine).
cron.info_engine: Jobs run automatically via the panel scheduler (every minute). Ensure /etc/cron.d/panelze-panel-scheduler is active on the server.
cron.info_paths: Use absolute paths in commands (php, wget, your site directory).
cron.examples_body:
# Schedule above (e.g. 0 * * * *). Command box is a shell line:

# Laravel
/usr/bin/php /var/www/site/public_html/artisan schedule:run >> /var/www/site/public_html/storage/logs/cron.log 2>&1

# CodeIgniter
cd /var/www/site/public_html/public && /usr/bin/php ../spark scrape:prices

# Allowed: && || ; | >> > 2>&1 # comment
# Blocked: `$(...)` backticks, multiline, paths outside your sites, curl|bash

ssh.port_desc: Custom port instead of 22, listen on internal networks only, align with firewall rules.

server.kernel_desc: KSplice / unattended-upgrades style flows and reboot windows (Pro).

website.modsec_intro: ModSecurity with OWASP CRS for Apache filters requests and bodies. On nginx-fronted stacks Apache must run as backend for this module.
website.toggle_hint: When you enable, if packages are missing the server will try to install libapache2-mod-security2 first, then turn the rule engine on.
website.per_site_desc: Per-virtualhost exceptions, sensitive paths, and custom CRS fragments (Pro).
website.crs_desc: False-positive tuning, custom rule bundles, and audit-only mode (Pro).

brute.intro: Fail2ban watches SSH and panel login attempts and temporarily bans IPs after too many failures.
brute.toggle_hint: Enable: if the package is missing, Fail2ban is installed via APT and the service is started.
brute.captcha_desc: Extra panel login protection and geo risk scoring (Pro).

compiler.intro: Disabling compilers on shared hosting makes post-exploit payload builds harder.
compiler.gcc_desc: Disable gcc, make, etc.; allow only in maintenance windows (Pro).
compiler.per_user_desc: Grant compile rights to selected system users (Pro).

attack.intro: Defence in depth: Nginx rate limits, IP reputation, and kernel SYN protection (Pro).
attack.bot_hint: Rate limit profiles and per-site ModSecurity rules help limit automated abuse.
attack.rate_desc: Per-request and per-IP limits, bursts, and location rules (Pro).
attack.ddos_desc: SYN handling, conntrack tuning, and kernel guidance (Pro).
attack.bot_desc: Flag suspicious automation and allow-list good bots (Pro).
attack.geo_desc: Country/ASN rules and real IP behind CDNs (Pro).

installer.subtitle: SMB: one-click scripts · Agency: deploy & Git · Modern stack: guides & tools
installer.page_stability_note: Do not refresh or leave this tab until the install request finishes; in sync queue mode the request may be cut off. If background workers are enabled, the install can continue after you leave — watch the “in progress” banner below.
installer.woocommerce_note: Plugin files go under wp-content/plugins; activate it in WP admin → Plugins after setup.
installer.opencart_automation_scope: Automated step: OpenCart files go to the document root. A password-free DB summary is written to domain/.panelze/opencart-db-hint.txt (usually outside public_html, not served over HTTP). Finish setup in the OpenCart web installer.
installer.opencart_automation_hint_short: Files are ready; complete the on-site OpenCart installer.
installer.guide_note_not_automated: Note: This app is not installed automatically in this version. The steps below guide you through a safe setup flow.
installer.guide_generic_step_1: First, verify the site root in the file manager (avoid installing into the wrong directory).
installer.guide_generic_step_2: If dependencies are required, use SSH or the Deploy screen.
installer.guide_deploy_step_1: In Deploy, pick domain, repository and branch, then run the first deployment (Node/Laravel/Next.js, etc.).
installer.guide_deploy_step_2: Fill build command, env vars and working directory to match your project.
installer.guide_laravel_step_1: For Laravel, the recommended web root is usually the `public/` directory.
installer.guide_laravel_step_2: Before installing, make sure the domain document root points to `public/` (otherwise it can be a security risk).
installer.guide_laravel_step_3: Run composer install in the document root via SSH.
installer.guide_laravel_step_4: If you use Deploy, set repo/branch/runtime and run a deploy.
installer.docroot_hint: For Laravel, the web root should usually be `public/`. This safely updates vhost and (if enabled) the PHP-FPM pool config (reversible).
installer.wordpress_automation_scope: Automated step: WordPress files and wp-config.php (with your database credentials) are written; MySQL tables are not created. The setup wizard you see in the browser is expected — finish language, admin user, and site details there.
installer.wordpress_automation_hint_short: Files are ready; complete the on-site setup wizard to create database tables.
installer.read_only_hint: You can only view installer features on this account. installer:write permission is required for changes.
